name: run terminal → ops-chain-observer
description: ADR-027 Phase 1, re-wired for the substrate-plus-overlays world. Fires once when a run reaches an absorbing phase and spawns one ops-chain-observer to diagnose the completed chain. Triggering on the RUN entity rather than on a reviewer role is what makes this category-agnostic: it covers research, autoresearch, and every future pack without re-authoring, and it covers failed and cancelled runs — the ones ops has the most to say about — which a reviewer-completion trigger structurally misses. Replaces chain-terminal-observe.json, whose `agent.loop.role eq reviewer-qa` trigger became dead config when ADR-041/042 retired that role.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.ops-chain-observer
on_enter.prompt:
A run has reached a terminal phase. Diagnose the chain that just finished.

**Run entity:** $entity.id
**Terminal phase:** $entity.triple.agent.run.phase

Start with query_entity on the run entity above — it carries the run's own facts. Walk to the member loops with query_relationships, and use read_loop_result on individual loops when you need what a role actually produced rather than that it finished.

You are looking for things an operator would want to know and cannot see from a green tick: a role that burned most of its iteration budget, a retry that succeeded but shouldn't have been needed, a phase that completed with thin output, a failure whose stated cause does not match its evidence. Ground every finding in graph entities you actually read.

Call emit_diagnosis once per finding, with evidence citing the entity IDs the finding rests on. **Finding nothing is the expected outcome on a healthy run** — do not manufacture a diagnosis to look useful. A clean run with zero emit_diagnosis calls is a correct and valuable observation.

Terminate with decide(action="observed", reason="<one line: what you examined and what you concluded>").

metadata.supersedes: configs/rules/ops/chain-terminal-observe.json (agent.loop.role eq reviewer-qa — role retired by ADR-041/042, so the rule could never fire) and configs/rules/ops/observe-chain-progress.json (see cadence_note).
metadata.cadence_note: Exactly one ops loop per run, set by trigger scope rather than by a throttle. `fire_every_n_events` does NOT gate publish_agent — upstream's shouldFireAction is only reached from fireRuleActions, while on_enter runs through the stateful evaluator, which never reads the counter (semstreams#1007). The retired observe-chain-progress.json declared `fire_every_n_events: 5` and would in fact have spawned one LLM loop per worker-loop completion.
metadata.cooldown_warning: Do NOT reach for `cooldown` as a per-entity throttle. It is per rule INSTANCE, so one entity's fire suppresses every other entity's, and suppression returns false from Evaluate — which the stateful evaluator reads as TransitionExited and therefore fires on_exit. Filed as part of semstreams#1007.
metadata.feedback_loop_safety: Four independent structural facts, no denylist to maintain: (1) run_scope none — the ops loop carries no RunID so it never joins the run it observes; (2) this rule fires on the run family while ops loops are loop-family entities; (3) all 32 wired loop-family rules gate on agent.loop.role and none names an ops role; (4) emit_diagnosis mints ops.diagnosis.finding entities that no wired rule's entity.pattern matches. Fact (4) is only true because of the ADR-059 narrowing — under the old blanket pattern every rule evaluated its conditions against every finding.
metadata.replay_note: Unlike agent-run/03, this condition stays true forever once a run terminates, so transition detection rests entirely on persisted MatchState. Clearing that KV while ENTITY_STATES survived would re-fire every historical run on boot. The standard `down -v` across the whole NATS store makes this unreachable; an operator doing selective bucket maintenance on long-lived NATS should switch to the `transition` operator (one target value per condition, so three terminals costs three rules).
metadata.subject_shape_note: Subject MUST be exactly two segments after `agent.task.` — agentic-dispatch subscribes on `agent.task.*`, a NATS single-token wildcard. Deeper subjects (e.g. `agent.task.ops.terminal_observe`) drop into the void: the rule fires, the action publishes, and no consumer subscribes. Smoke #8 run-11 surfaced this the hard way.
metadata.no_submit_work: The retired rules granted `submit_work`, which does not exist upstream — no executor, no registration, only a category-map entry and comments (semstreams#1007). Unknown tool names are logged and dropped, so the personas were instructing a tool the model never received. Terminal is decide(action=observed), gated by action_allowlist.
